title: RAW development and qualification
objective: Make RAW development fast and simple — one tile executor on the shared pool, normalization in Rust, a GainMap without repeated weights, a measured source-cache policy, a narrow safe develop boundary, one container parser, a trimmed public API and tooling — and finish the qualification of continuous RAW editing for the Nikon Z6, Fujifilm X100VI and DJI Air 2S.
context_summary: Continuous RAW editing is implemented: LibRaw decodes a retained u16 mosaic; Rust normalizes it and scales the planes, and the pinned librtprocess RCD and Markesteijn only demosaic; the native tile jobs and the Rust development passes share one refill executor on the shared pool; the DNG GainMap derives its taps once per row and column; and one verified source cache with single-flight preparation keyed by gains feeds the renderer, keeps a second development within a 600 MiB budget and evicts only for queued work that allocates planes. What remains of the engineering work is structure: a narrower develop FFI boundary, one container parser, a trimmed public API and the finished RAW tooling. The RAW qualification milestone's tasks (controlled quality, the foundation and journey checkpoints, failure hardening, packaging and whole-editor measurement) run beside the engineering waves; RAW export is delivered. Decisions: docs/decisions.md "Post-consolidation review"; constraints: docs/design/post-consolidation.md; RAW contracts: docs/design/initial-raw.md, raw-integration.md, air2s-dng.md.

tasks.description: Delete the process-wide native scratch semaphore and its timed waits from `luxforge-raw`, keeping each development's own lane cap, and remove the semaphore's test lock and permit tests with it.
extra_context: Wave 1, fix. The semaphore is dead weight production cannot contend, and it is also a load-dependent test's only reason to exist; deleting it removes the failure class instead of patching one instance of it.

`native_tiles.rs` holds a static 8-slot semaphore (`SLOTS`, `admit`, `ScratchPermit`, `PEAK_SLOTS`, `TEST_BUDGET_LOCK`) with the RAW path's only timed waits: a 1 ms `park_timeout` loop for Rayon callers and a 20 ms timed condvar wait for everyone else. In production it can never block: `RawSource::develop` runs only on the single source worker, which already waits on the plane gate for every earlier development's planes to release before it starts the next, and each call already caps its own concurrency at 8 or fewer lanes.

`native_tiles::tests::rayon_waiter_runs_queued_permit_release_in_a_one_thread_pool` asserted `permit.count == MAX_SCRATCH_SLOTS` as 7 instead of 8 twice inside a full `cargo test --locked --workspace` run, and passed every time it ran alone. Its own `PEAK_SLOTS == MAX_SCRATCH_SLOTS` assertion only reads a process-wide high-water mark that the same test's first admission of all 8 slots already set, so it is unconditionally true and proves nothing about the executor.
Keep the per-call lane cap (8 today) and the plane gate that already serializes developments; only the global slot counter, its timed waits and its test-only lock go.

tasks.description: Replace the native tile executor's joined batches with one refill scope, also used by the Rust development passes, so no job waits for a batch's slowest one and at most eight tiles of work are ever open to stealing.
extra_context: Wave 3, speed. Once the semaphore is gone, the remaining scheduling cost is a serialized tail job plus joined batches, on every development.

The long dependent tail job runs inside the executor's first scope, so every other job waits for it; the remaining jobs then run in batches of at most 8, each batch joined before the next starts, so every batch waits for its slowest job. On the Z6 (RCD, 805 tiles, 110 jobs, a 38-tile tail) that models 36-49 ms against a measured 40.8 ms; on the X100VI (Markesteijn, 4,293 tiles, 562 jobs, a 162-tile tail) it models about 200-275 ms. A refill schedule is estimated at about 25-28 ms for the Z6 and 150-165 ms for the X100VI.

The same at-most-eight-tiles-of-stealable-work rule the executor exists for is not applied to the Rust passes that run on the same pool: DNG correction rows (`dng.rs`) and camera-conversion chunks (core `source.rs`) both run a plain adaptive parallel iterator over the whole frame instead.

Give every spawned task one job, then have it re-spawn itself to pull the next index from a shared counter; the caller runs the tail job first, then pulls ordinary jobs itself until none remain. Offer the same executor to the Rust passes, or record a measurement that justifies leaving them on a plain parallel iterator.
Cancellation between jobs and the tail's serial position both stay; every job still starts at a full tile with fresh scratch, so bytes cannot change.

tasks.description: Move RAW mosaic normalization and the post-demosaic /65535 scale into Rust on the development pool, so the native `lf_raw_develop` call only demosaics.
extra_context: Wave 3, speed. Normalization and the output scale are serial full-frame work on the single source thread today; moving them into Rust removes duplicated C++ and lets them run on the pool this plan just gave a refill schedule.

X-Trans normalization is never parallel in `adapter.cpp`: `normalize_rows` batches only when `meta->cfa_width == 2` (Bayer); X-Trans always takes the serial loop below it. The Bayer serial cost was measured at 39.5 ms at 24.5 MP, which projects to about 65-90 ms at the X100VI's 40.9 MP. Both loops divide `65535 / (white - black)` per pixel and re-check invariants `interpret` already validated at decode. `std::vector<float> mosaic(count)` zero-fills the normalized mosaic (491 MB on the X100VI) before either loop overwrites it, and a final serial loop divides all three planes by 65535 after the demosaic.
`neutral.rs` keeps a third copy of the same per-site black-level model, in f64, for the neutral picker.

Precompute the same per-site `black` and `65535.0 / (white - black)` values C++ computes per pixel, evaluate `(sample - black) * k * gain` in the same order for Bayer and X-Trans alike, and divide the planes by 65535 in parallel chunks as soon as the native call returns, still ahead of the DNG corrections so the order of operations is kept. The neutral picker reuses the site-to-black lookup instead of keeping its own copy.
Bytes must not change: keep the same IEEE f32 subtraction, division and multiplications in the same order, with no `a*b+c` shape a compiler could contract into an FMA.

tasks.description: Precompute the DNG GainMap's row and column weights once per row and column instead of recomputing them for every pixel and channel.
extra_context: Wave 3, speed. This is now the Air 2S's largest development stage, since pooled RCD already made the native demosaic itself fast.

`Warp::apply`'s per-pixel loop calls `GainMap::gain` once per stage, per channel, per pixel; on the Air 2S active area (5472x3648, about 20 million pixels) that is about 60 million calls. Each call re-derives `fy`, `y0` and `wy` from the row alone, and `fx`, `x0` and `wx` from the column alone, then re-does the same bounds checks, clamps and floors every time.

Precompute `(x0, x1, wx)` once per column and `(y0, y1, wy)` once per row for each stage, and evaluate the same bilinear expression per channel; keep `(pixel as f64 * gain) as f32` exactly as it is today.
Same f64 operands, same operations, same order: the corrected mosaic is byte-identical by construction, not by re-verification alone.

tasks.description: Evict the cached RAW development only when a queued task will allocate new planes, then measure the hold-`\` compare on the X100VI and add a byte-budgeted second slot or a proxy-only compare if a switch still costs more than about 150 ms.
extra_context: Wave 3, speed. The eviction rule costs whole redevelopments on ordinary Lightroom-familiar gestures; the owner's decision on a second development slot waits for this task's own measurement of what this plan's other RAW speedups leave behind.

`queue_preparation` and the completion path in the owner evict the cached development for any strict evaluation at other gains: selecting a history entry, holding `\` to compare against the Original (two redevelopments per toggle), or another client's sample or analysis of a different entry. Measured before this plan's speed work: Historical Original to captured frame p50 507 ms (Z6), 1,559 ms (X100VI), 1,484 ms (Air 2S); Return to current 491, 1,616, 1,523; a 100% view change costs about 25 ms by comparison on every camera. A completed source job also evicts a just-installed development whenever any other job is active, artifact-only reads included.

Memory (CPU bytes, at 18 B/px: u16 mosaic + f32 normalized mosaic + f32 planes): a development peaks at 441 MB on the Z6 and 736 MB on the X100VI; steady displayed is about 510/810 MB; a white-balance-release peak is about 0.61/0.97 GB. Two float developments never coexist; the plane gate enforces that and stays untouched. The crate's 128 MP pixel limit binds before its 1.5 GiB per-buffer limit; at that cap a development peaks at about 2.3 GB before any RGBA.

The owner's decision: keep one RAW development per process until this task and the executor and normalization changes land, then measure the hold-`\` compare on the X100VI; if a switch still costs more than about 150 ms, add a byte-budgeted second development slot (for example 600 MB or less) or a compare that shows only the other entry's proxy while the exact frame redevelops. A byte-budgeted cache that also keeps JPEG decodes beside the one RAW development follows only after a separate RSS measurement on the M4.

Fix the eviction rule regardless of which option follows the measurement: evict only when a queued task allocates new planes (a File or Develop job), not on every artifact-only job in the flight table.

tasks.description: Narrow the RAW develop FFI boundary: one crate-private `develop_with(options)` in place of the forwarding chain, a small shape struct instead of the whole decode metadata, generated status codes and no test fault injector in the production ABI.
extra_context: Wave 4, structure. The decode half of the boundary is already minimal and stays as it is; only the develop half is wider than its job.

Already in place: normalization and the /65535 scale run in Rust (`normalize.rs`: `Normalization`, `BlackLevels`, `scale_planes`), so `lf_raw_develop` only demosaics and the normalized-mosaic capture hook is gone. `native_demosaic` in `lib.rs` holds the one unsafe `lf_raw_develop` call, used by production (`develop_uncorrected_diagnostic`) and the tests (`develop_synthetic`, and the Markesteijn fault and cancellation cases in `markesteijn_parallel_complete_float_oracle`). Development timing is a Rust-side `DevelopDiagnostics`, not an ABI pointer.

Still wider than its job: `lf_raw_develop` takes 13 positional arguments and the whole decode `NativeMetadata`, 4,096-value black-repeat table included, although the demosaic reads only the dimensions, the CFA shape and pattern and, for Markesteijn, `rgb_cam`. The `test_fault` injector sits in the production signature and is forwarded into the patched librtprocess (`testFault` in `patches/librtprocess-local.patch`); `rcd_job_faults_join_and_release_scratch` and the Markesteijn oracle's fault cases use it. Status codes 1-7 are literals on both sides, matched by hand in `native_error`. Four forwarding functions (`develop_uncorrected`, `develop_uncorrected_with_workers`, `develop_uncorrected_diagnostic` and the `performance-diagnostics` feature's `develop_for_performance_diagnostic`) carry three knobs: the worker limit, whether the development executor runs, and the diagnostics.

Add one crate-private `develop_with(options)` in place of that chain. Its options carry the worker limit and the executor choice that both lane rules read (`native_tiles::native_lanes`, at most eight, for the native jobs; `development_lanes`, the pool's width, for the Rust passes on `native_tiles::refill` and `refill_each`), plus the optional diagnostics. Keep `native_demosaic` the one unsafe call and give `lf_raw_develop` a shape struct (dimensions, CFA kind and pattern, `rgb_cam`) instead of `NativeMetadata`, which then serves only the decode. Generate a status enum into the header `build.rs` already writes for the limits (`camera_allowlist.h`), mapped in one match. Keep native fault injection for the tests without a production parameter, for example through a test-only entry point or a fault raised by the Rust executor's job callback.

Keep every caller working through the new entry: the ignored release profiles `owner_development_timing` and `bayer_normalization_release_abba_profile`, the core's ignored contention diagnostics in `render/linear.rs` that call `develop_for_performance_diagnostic`, and the second development, whose read-back core's ignored `supplied_raw_preparation_keeps_its_pinned_bits` checks against the pinned development digests.

tasks.description: Parse every TIFF/DNG container with one IFD walk and one byte-reader set, merge the two opcode modules, share one 3x3 matrix helper, and parse DNG opcode lists only for DNG files.
extra_context: Wave 4, structure. Three walks over the same untrusted structure, each bounded slightly differently, are copies that drift apart; one walk is one set of bounds to get right.

`format.rs` walks IFDs three times (`dng_opcodes`, `dng_container`, `dng_color_calibration`), each with its own SubIFD-offset decoding, and the three do not agree on whether a zero offset or a zero SubIFD count is allowed. `dng_ops.rs` is a second, isolated module with its own error type (`OpcodeError`) and its own byte readers, adapted by `dng.rs` rather than sharing `RawError` and one reader set. "Required opcode IDs" (filter by the optional flag, collect, sort, dedup) is written three times: in `lib.rs`'s `reject_unhandled_required_opcodes` and `RawSource::decode`, and in `format.rs`'s `required_dng_opcodes`. The same 3x3 cofactor-expansion determinant is written out four times: `lib.rs`'s `validate_camera_response` and `interpret`, `format.rs` and `profiles.rs`. `RawSource::decode` parses DNG opcode lists for every TIFF-magic RAW file, NEF included, before `lf_raw_open`, though only DNG needs them.

Write one `Tiff::walk(first, limit, |ifd, entries| ...)` with one bounds policy; merge `dng_ops.rs` into `dng.rs` on `RawError` and one reader set, keeping `dng.rs`'s GainMap taps and its correction rows on the development executor (`native_tiles::refill_each`) as they are; write one `required_ids` helper; add a small `mat3` helper that `build.rs` includes the way it already includes `limits`, `opcodes` and `profiles`; gate opcode-list parsing on LibRaw reporting a DNG version, which moves the parse after `lf_raw_open`.

This reorganizes the Rust-side parsing that already runs after LibRaw's own unpack; it does not touch or replace that unpack. Replacing LibRaw's unpack with RawSpeed is a separate proposal awaiting the owner and is out of scope here.

Malformed-input edge behavior (for example a zero SubIFD offset) may change where the three walks disagreed; every existing malformed-input case, in both the unit tests and the real-file suite, must still resolve the same way or fail explicitly, never silently.

Outstanding: evidence only. The walk, readers, merged opcode module, `mat3` and the DNG-only opcode parse are in place; the walk rejects a zero SubIFD offset and a zero or over-eight SubIFD count in every caller. The owner files pass the real-file suite, and 18 files (the owner's three and 15 raw.pixls.us CC0 files over nine formats) qualify through `qualify_profiles` with results identical to the base commit. The real-file suite's public CC0 case and the qualifier over the whole 100-camera catalog have not run: neither the four named CC0 files nor a 100-camera qualifier manifest is on the owner's M4.

tasks.description: Trim `luxforge-raw`'s public API to what `luxforge-core`, `xtask` and the crate's own example use, beside the limits module's shared items, and replace the generated 103-variant `RawMode` enum with a validated static reference into the camera catalog.
extra_context: Wave 4, structure. A public surface wider than its consumers, and a generated enum matched on only as a string, are both maintenance cost with no behavior behind them.

Unused or crate-only public items: `RawSource::mosaic_arc` has no caller; `mosaic_corrections` has none outside the crate; `corrected_sensor_sample_location` and `gain_at_corrected_sensor` are used by the neutral picker (`neutral.rs`) and the real-file suite; `required_dng_opcodes` is re-exported for `real_files.rs` alone. `RawSource::mosaic` stays public for `examples/qualify_profiles.rs`.

Public by design, not to trim: the limits module's cross-crate items, which exist so `luxforge-core` imports each bound from its one home (repository rule `render-limits-home`): the admission limits, `MAX_FRAME_BYTES`, `PARALLEL_PIXELS`, the per-pass threshold table (`RenderPass`, `parallel_pixels` and its `PARALLEL_*_PIXELS` constants, all but `PARALLEL_TRANSFORM_PIXELS` and `PARALLEL_PROXY_PIXELS` named by core), the spatial tile rule (`spatial_tile`, `SPATIAL_TILE`, `SPATIAL_WIDE_TILE`, `SPATIAL_WIDE_HALO`) and `RETAINED_DEVELOPMENT_BYTES`, the second development's budget in core's `source.rs`; and `refill_each`, the development executor core's camera conversion (`source.rs`) runs its chunks on. `develop_for_performance_diagnostic` is public only under the `performance-diagnostics` feature, for core's ignored diagnostics; the develop-boundary task in this plan decides how it reaches the development.

`build.rs` generates `RawMode` into `raw_modes.rs` (103 variants over the 100-camera catalog, with a generated `id` match); production uses it only through its serde form and `requires_dng_corrections`, which scans the catalog, and `RawSource::interpret` builds one by writing the matched mode's id as JSON and parsing it back. The same build script already generates the catalog itself as static Rust data (`camera_catalog.rs`), so a `&'static` mode is a lookup away.

Make the unused and crate-only items crate-private, moving their real-file assertions into `dng.rs`'s and `format.rs`'s own tests; replace the enum with `RawMode(&'static Mode)`, deserialized by catalog lookup, with `requires_dng_corrections` read from the mode's camera instead of a catalog scan. The generated `raw_modes.rs` and the JSON round trip both go. Callers that name a variant construct by id instead: `xtask/src/raw.rs`'s manifest entries (through serde), core's `editor/test_support.rs` and the tests in `editor/source.rs` and `render/linear.rs`, `real_files.rs` and `profiles.rs`'s tests.

tasks.description: Measure full-editor RAW responsiveness, memory and JPEG regressions on the owner's M4.
extra_context: RAW qualification milestone on the roadmap, not a wave of the post-consolidation work.
This measurement is taken after the development executor, the Rust normalization and the second development landed, so the recorded distributions describe the code that ships.
Provisional time/RSS targets are investigation hypotheses until the owner accepts measured budgets. Do not hide misses by changing input modes or quietly enabling embedded previews.

Tools: the RAW editor journey is the `raw-editor` smoke scenario, which records one functional run's request-to-display and capture times per source in `raw-editor-checks.json`, so a distribution is 30 runs of it; RAW memory under a heavy edit is the `performance` scenario's over a RAW `--source`; below the editor, `luxforge-raw`'s ignored release tests `owner_development_timing` (development and DNG corrections) and `bayer_normalization_release_abba_profile` (normalization against demosaic) time the development's own stages. JPEG baselines use editor-performance.

Recorded before waves 1 to 3 (docs/specs/performance.md, "Current RAW and JPEG measurements"): thirty complete native M4 trials per owner camera and four public mode workflows pass; the same 24/60 MP JPEG core diagnostic is recorded before/after; Fuji captured RSS p95 is 1992 MiB with an unexplained 2436 MiB maximum, and screenshot-free peaks are 1583-1647 MiB. Those history rows predate the refill executor, the Rust normalization and the second development.

Current figures, on a shared host: retained-mosaic development p50 is about 184-232 ms on the X100VI, 37-40 ms on the Z6 and 31-34 ms on the Air 2S ("Mosaic normalization"); a switch whose development the second slot holds displays in about 20 ms p50 on the X100VI and Air 2S and about 32 ms on the Z6, and holding both developments adds 230 to 458 MiB of RSS, the X100VI's edit launch reaching 2290 / 2352 MiB p50 / p95 over the switch window ("Second development"). A redevelopment's peak also holds the retained development. Fine-grained stage/GPU/cancellation/idle attribution and an accepted budget remain open.

The owner decided the RAW memory budget on 2026-09-28 (docs/decisions.md, "Plan refresh"): the one-development working set keeps its 1.5 GiB CPU-RSS investigation target until this measurement attributes today's miss, and the retained second development has its own 600 MiB byte budget (`luxforge_raw::RETAINED_DEVELOPMENT_BYTES`), with GPU memory reported separately. Only this task's numbers count against it; if a measured total is unacceptable, propose a higher target, a smaller slot or a proxy-only compare. This task's M4 RSS measurement is also the one the second-development decision names before any byte-budgeted source cache that keeps JPEG decodes beside the RAW developments, and the GPU residency measurement beyond the photo-texture ceiling runs beside it.

Measurement depends on the implemented editor, not on completion of broad controlled-scene/fuzz/portability gates. Those gates remain independently open. RSS sampling includes renderer/capture effects and must not be relabelled as isolated CPU heap or GPU memory.
